data.long_meaning: Derived from the Irish name 'Tadhg Ruadh', meaning 'Tadhg the red'. Tadhg is derived from the Celtic word 'tadh', meaning 'god' or 'father'. The name Tyrone is believed to have been anglicized from 'Tir Eoghain', which means 'land of Eoghan'. The name Tyrone carries the meaning “Tire's town” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English. Parents who choose Tyrone usually hope their child will grow to embody tire's town and live with faith, good character and purpose.
